name: F#
title: F# (9)

type.text: **Discriminated unions separate cases**: Like Haskell ADTs
**Type providers decouple data access from code**: SQL, JSON, etc. accessed via types generated from schemas
**OOP interop allows inheritance coupling**: Can use C# classes with inheritance and other C# patterns, coupling subclasses to base classes
**Nulls from .NET**: Nullable references from C# libraries reintroduce null-checking coupling

construction.text: **Immutable records by default**: Construction doesn't couple to mutation
**With-copy syntax decouples updates**: `{ person with Age = 30 }` doesn't modify original
**Can use .NET constructors with side effects**: Interop allows coupled construction
**Mutable cells exist**: Can create ref cells, coupling to mutable state

memory.text: **.NET GC decouples memory**: Generational GC handles deallocation
**Immutability simplifies GC**: Fewer mutable references, cleaner collection
**GC pauses affect latency**: Non-deterministic pauses, though .NET GC is mature
**Can use IDisposable from .NET**: Manual resource management via `use` keyword couples cleanup
**Garbage collection handles closures**: Captured references are traced by the .NET GC, not by reference counting

error.text: **Result type separates success/failure**: `Result<'T, 'Error>` makes errors explicit
**Can throw .NET exceptions**: Interop allows unchecked exceptions
**Railway-oriented programming pattern**: The community embraces this functional error-handling style where success and failure paths are composed like parallel railroad tracks using Result types

concurrency.text: **Async workflows decouple async from sync**: `async { }` blocks separate concerns
**MailboxProcessor for actors**: Message passing decouples concurrent operations
**.NET threads allow shared mutable state**: Interop permits coupling

platform.text: **Cross-platform .NET runtime**: The same F# assembly runs on Linux, macOS, and Windows
**Open-source compiler**: The F# compiler (dotnet/fsharp) is MIT-licensed and developed in the open as a .NET Foundation project
**Freely available, cross-platform toolchain**: The `dotnet` SDK and NuGet run on Linux, macOS, and Windows at no cost, and Visual Studio is optional rather than required
**Multiple compile targets**: Fable compiles F# to JavaScript, so the language reaches the browser as well as the .NET runtime

performance.text: **Tail call optimization**: Decouples recursion from stack size
**Immutability optimized**: Persistent data structures perform well
**Startup time**: JIT warmup couples cold start to performance

ecosystem.text: **Excellent IDE support**: Visual Studio, Rider, VSCode with Ionide
**Some .NET libraries couple to OOP patterns**: Not all libraries are functional-friendly
**CLR metadata carries a published promise**: F# compiles to IL under the runtime's standardised format [@ecma335; @dotnetCompat]

**Stored payloads bind to the runtime**: F# runs on the .NET runtime, and from .NET 8 BinaryFormatter throws across nearly all project types, with .NET 9 removing the in-box implementation [@netBinFmtDisabled; @netBinFmtRemoved]

evolution.text: **Strong backward compatibility**: Code rarely breaks between versions
**Active development**: Regular improvements and new features
**Coupled to .NET platform evolution**: Must follow .NET's direction

domain.text: **Excellent for backend services**: Async, type safety, .NET performance
**Strong for data analysis**: Type providers for data access
**Great for financial/scientific**: Immutability, correctness, units of measure
**Web frontend less common**: Fable exists but smaller ecosystem than mainstream

learning.text: **Gentler than Haskell**: More pragmatic, less abstract
**Good docs**: F# for Fun and Profit, official docs
**Requires functional mindset shift**: For OOP developers
**Can adopt gradually**: Mix FP and OOP as needed

syntax.text: **Type inference limitations**: Sometimes need explicit annotations

testing.text: **Excellent debugger**: Visual Studio debugger is world-class
**Pure functions easy to test**: No hidden state

security.text: **Immutability by default**: Prevents many mutation bugs
**C# interop escape hatches**: `mutable`, `null`, unsafe code possible

tradeoffs: **Functional Purity vs. .NET Interop**: Can't enforce purity when calling C# code
**Type Safety vs. Practical Libraries**: .NET libraries use null, exceptions, mutation—F# must accommodate
**Railway-Oriented Programming vs. Exceptions**: Community promotes Result types but .NET uses exceptions
**Immutability by Default vs. Performance**: Persistent data structures slower than .NET mutable collections
**FP Culture vs. OOP Platform**: F# encourages FP but runs on OOP-first platform
verdict: F# provides excellent coupling-reducing features (discriminated unions, Result, async, immutability) but .NET interop creates escape hatches. Pragmatic trade-off: coupling when you want it, C# compatibility when needed. Main weakness: discipline required to avoid .NET coupling traps.

energy.text: Runs on a virtual machine, above native code in the energy and time benchmarks [@pereira2017energy]; a causal re-analysis attributes most of the gap to execution time [@vankempen2025green].

ai-readiness.text: Moderate training data: models write it competently, with measurable language-specific weakness [@joel2025lowresource].

safety.text: No certified or standards-qualified path for safety-critical systems.

delivery.note: IL and assembly metadata follow a published standard, and the runtime publishes its compatibility rules

data_formats.note: Microsoft states that BinaryFormatter.Serialize and BinaryFormatter.Deserialize throw NotSupportedException at runtime across nearly all project types starting in .NET 8, and that in .NET 9 the in-box implementation throws on use even with the settings that previously enabled it, because those settings are removed
